Staff is aware of mercury spill management

1. Ensure staff are trained in mercury spill management procedures, including immediate evacuation of the spill area to prevent exposure.  
2. Instruct staff to remove all jewelry before handling mercury to avoid contamination.  
3. Ensure staff are wearing the necessary personal protective equipment (PPE), such as gloves, masks, and eye protection.  
4. Provide staff with flashlights to locate mercury beads in dark or low-visibility areas.  
5. Ensure staff use proper tools, such as a syringe without a needle or an eyedropper, and sticky tape to safely collect the mercury beads.  
6. Collect the mercury beads in leak-proof bags or containers to prevent further contamination.  
7. Ensure staff are trained to sprinkle sulfur or zinc powder to remove any remaining mercury residue.  
8. Verify that all spill surfaces are decontaminated with a 10% sodium thiosulfate solution to neutralize mercury.  
9. Ensure all bags or containers containing mercury-contaminated items are clearly marked as "Hazardous Waste

Staff aware of mercury spill management

Staff aware of mercury spill management :
1. Spill area evacuation
2. Removal of Jewellery
3. Wear PPE 
4. Use of flashlight to lacate mercury beads
5. Use syringe without a needle/eyedropper and sticky tape to suck the beads
6. Collection of beads in leak-proof bag or container
7. Sprinkle sulphur or zinc powder to remove any remaining mercury
8. All the mercury spill surfaces should be decontaminated with 10% sodium thiosulfate solution
9. All the bags or containers containing items contaminated with mercury should be marked as “Hazardous Waste, Handle with Care”
10. Collected mercury waste should be handed over to the CBMWTF
